title: Rank-zero Rees specialization and integration in section coordinates
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\ge1$, and $A=\mathbb Z/\ell^n$ in the coefficient universe. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated, etale, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and compactifiable between Noetherian schemes, with $\ell$ invertible at every stalk of both schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-asd-compactifiable]. Let $N$ be a family of compact-support/sum comparisons satisfying the graph and homotopy normalization equations [def-pur-finite-smooth-comparison-coordinates]. Use the unchanged coordinate and factor constructions [def-pur-finite-smooth-gamma-constructions]. There exists $G:\mathrm{FiniteSmoothGammaData}(A,f)$ such that finiteSmoothDeformationFactor followed by finiteSmoothNormalCoordinates equals finiteSmoothSectionCoordinates for the first projection and the diagonal, and finiteSmoothRankZeroFactor equals finiteSmoothNormalCoordinates. Both are equalities of the specified morphisms; no diagonal-factor or tensor-map equation is asserted.

proof.text: The diagonal is a section of the etale separated first projection. It is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. On its image the ideal is zero and on its complement it is the unit ideal. Thus the conormal has rank zero and the actual normal projection is an isomorphism. The required regular sequence near the section is the empty sequence. Base-change and Noetherian permanence give the asserted hypotheses.

proof.text:
Compute the rank-zero deformation directly from its definition in [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization]. On $\Delta(X)$ the ideal is zero, so the Rees subalgebra is $\mathcal O_X[t]$. On $V_0$ it is $\mathcal O_{V_0}$, so adjoining $\mathcal I/t$ adjoins $t^{-1}$, and the algebra is $\mathcal O_{V_0}[t,t^{-1}]$. The two pieces are disjoint open and closed pieces of $W$, so these calculations give
$$D=\mathbf A^1_X\amalg(V_0\times\mathbf G_m),$$
with $\widetilde g$ equal to the identity on the first component and to the restriction of $p_1\times1$ on the second. The deformed section is the inclusion of the first component. The fibre at $1$ is $W$ with section $\Delta$; at $0$ only the first component remains, giving $(X,1_X)$. These identifications send $t$ to the base parameter and preserve the section; they are the fibre identifications of the defining Rees algebra.

proof.text: Here are the hypotheses for the specialization theorem, before using its conclusion. The component $V_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The map $\widetilde g$ in Step 4 is etale: on the first component it is the identity, and on the second it is the base change of $p_1$ followed by restriction to an open subscheme, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is separated and finite type: $W\times\mathbf A^1\to\mathbf A^1_X$ has these properties by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; the displayed $D$ is its open subscheme obtained by deleting $V_0\times\{0\}$. Restriction preserves the locally finite-type affine presentations, and quasi-compactness follows from the Noetherian open-subscheme lemma. Its relative diagonal is the restriction of the ambient closed diagonal, hence is closed. The ambient scheme and $\mathbf A^1_X$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and $D$ is Noetherian by the open-subscheme lemma. All have $\ell$ invertible by pullback. Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Therefore [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to $p_1$, $\widetilde g$ and $\pi=1_X$. They are compactifiable. Etaleness gives smooth relative dimension zero by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and Step 2 gives the required regular closed section.

proof.text: Apply the coordinates of Step 1 to the three etale maps $p_1$, $\widetilde g$ and $\pi$. Thus $C=\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}=A_X$ and $F=\widetilde\Delta^*\omega_{\widetilde g}=A_{\mathbf A^1_X}$. Step 3 at the inclusions $t=1,0$ says that the canonical exceptional fibre comparisons are the identity unit comparisons. Consequently the identity $A_{\mathbf A^1_X}\to a^*A_X$ is an isomorphism $F\to a^*C$ whose fibre at $1$ is $1_C$ under exactly the specified fibre maps. The uniqueness clause of [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization] forces $\kappa_{p_1,\Delta}$ to be this map. Restricting at $0$ and inverting proves $\delta_{p_1,\Delta}=1_{A_X}$. No assertion about an unspecified locality isomorphism is used to determine this scalar.

proof.text: For the identity projection, the rank-zero clause of [def-amb-vector-integration] is the identity-adjunction trace. The definition finiteSmoothRankZeroFactor already uses this trace, transported by the normal projection and zero section through the specified exceptional section map. Graph and homotopy normalization fix the compact-support comparison at the identity. Right-adjoint uniqueness therefore identifies its final identity-adjunction factor with the sum-adjunction coordinate. The exceptional mate preserves that coordinate by the sum-exchange counit equation, so the transported rank-zero factor is exactly finiteSmoothNormalCoordinates. This proves the last displayed equality without invoking a positive-rank or coefficient-field vector-bundle purity theorem.

theorem finiteSmoothDeformation_coordinates
    (ell n : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (ell : X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (ell : Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [Etale f] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasCompactification f]
    (N : FiniteSmoothCompactSupportComparisons (NoetherianSectionSpecialization.Coeff ell n))
    (hN : FiniteSmoothComparisonNormalized (NoetherianSectionSpecialization.Coeff ell n) N) :
    ∃ G : FiniteSmoothGammaData (NoetherianSectionSpecialization.Coeff ell n) f,
      finiteSmoothDeformationFactor _ f G ≫ (finiteSmoothNormalCoordinates _ N f G).hom =
          (finiteSmoothSectionCoordinates _ N (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f)).hom ∧
        finiteSmoothRankZeroFactor _ f G = (finiteSmoothNormalCoordinates _ N f G).hom
